quest.title: Medicine Born of Guilt
quest.description: In the first half of the exhibition match, Kachina seems to have something on her mind. Go and ask her about it.
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Mora x40000, Hero's Wit x3

chapter.num: Tournament of Glory in Bloom: Act II
chapter.title: Medicine Born of Guilt

talks.objective: Go to the Children of Echoes to find Kachina

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, here you are, Kachina!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Oh, hey... I had some time on my hands, so I decided to bring Ayo over to check on Milray and Naiyan.

dialogues.speaker: Ayo
dialogues.text: Roooah...

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: Oorooo...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Don't worry, everything's gonna be fine!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Huh? What makes you ask?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, you seemed a bit down after the exhibition match, so we're kinda worried about you.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: #Thanks, {NICKNAME} and Paimon. I'm okay, really. I mean, it's hard to explain. I've just... been feeling a bit lost.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Despite losing the Pilgrimage so many times, what kept me going was the belief that someday I'd win and earn a spot in the Night Warden Wars.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: So when I finally did, I was over the moon! I mean, things didn't exactly go as planned, and you and the others had to rescue me from the Night Kingdom...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: ...Still, I achieved my dream. But after the happiness wore off, I felt... hollow. I didn't know what to aim for next, or what I should work toward.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Then the Bloomflower Trials came around, and I could fight alongside everyone again. But when the exhibition match ended, I suddenly realized that everyone had "real-life" responsibilities to return to... Everyone, that is, except for me.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: And that got me thinking... Am I the only one who's still like a kid? The only one who's left with so much free time on their hands, who's never really grown up?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's what's been bothering you, huh?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This is an important stage in life, too, Kachina.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Huh? You mean... Everyone feels like this at some point? I thought it was just because I hadn't been working hard enough...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: #Oh... I see! Thank you, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, if you think about it, this is a good thing! Not knowing what you want means the future's still full of possibilities, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When Paimon can't decide what she wants for dinner, she gets to imagine all kinds of delicious dishes!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But if someone told her, "You're eating this tonight," it kinda spoils the anticipation.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: That actually makes a lot of sense!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I see even you have your moments of wisdom, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, stop underestimating Paimon like that, would'ja?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Oh, looks like you guys beat me to it. Is the little guy feeling any better?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Granny Citlali! H—Hello!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hello. I didn't have much going on at the moment, so I thought I'd check in on our patient.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Milray's been in a deep sleep this whole time... It's just as Ifa said. We'll need to gather all the Sacred Flame Crystals before we can help him.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I imagine you're right...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: *ahem* By the way, you haven't run into any trouble lately, have you?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: When we discussed the Sacred Flame Crystals after the exhibition match ended, everyone else looked happy, but you seemed to have something on your mind.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Ah, so that's what this is about... I was worried that the Sacred Flame Crystals might be dangerous. Did she think there was something else on my mind...?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (While I was worrying about Kachina, she was worrying about me... I should just be honest with her about the rumor.)

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Citlali about the rumor that Sacred Flame Crystals can "beguile human hearts."

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: A baseless rumor... but a fearful-sounding one all the same. Fear stems from the unknown, so the more cryptic the hearsay, the more panic it spreads.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Wait, are the Crystals actually dangerous? Then what about Milray?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Mavuika was right. Even if trouble does come our way, she'll handle it.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Still, there must be a story behind the Bloomflower Trials being stopped. It is said that something "happened" the last time they were held...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Since you're concerned, why don't we look into it? I'm sure we'll still be able to find scrolls from back then over at the Masters of the Night-Wind.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: C—Can I come along? I'd like to help!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I don't see why not. Come, let's head over to my place. We should leave this little Tepetlisaur to rest.

choices.text: Knowing the truth will put our minds at ease.
Take your time searching for what it is you want to do.
Has something been on your mind lately?

talks.objective: Go to the Masters of the Night-Wind to investigate the ancient woven scrolls

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I had someone gather up all the woven scrolls from that era. Maybe we'll find some leads we can follow.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: There's... There's... that many!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is gonna take forever!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Come on — less whining, more reading. If we split them up, we'll finish in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (A variety of events are recorded in these scrolls, like moments of frozen history with the power to pull you back into the distant past.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I've flipped through several of them, but still, nothing about the Bloomflower Trials. Yet the stories they contain... They're almost unimaginable.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (War, peace, alliances, betrayals... Seems like in the Natlan of six or seven centuries past, relations between the six tribes were incredibly complex and constantly shifting.)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Why've you stopped? Did you notice something strange?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are there still conflicts between the tribes nowadays?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: There will always be tensions, but the intensity has changed.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Usually, the Pyro Archon tries their best to prevent inter-tribal disputes from escalating. But not every Archon has done that as well as Mavuika.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Also, given that our Archons live only as long as mortals, the transitional periods can be fraught with challenges.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Far fewer conflicts have ended in bloodshed over the past few centuries. Whenever I read through these scrolls, I too am always struck by the thought of how unimaginable our lives would seem to people back then.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Hey, come check this out! This one seems to mention the Bloomflower Trials!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Oh? Let me see...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hmm... A curious coincidence indeed.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: It seems like the last Bloomflower Trials were also held to save the life of an ailing saurian.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Huh? Was it the same illness as Milray's?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: The scroll doesn't say, but it seems likely.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Strange... It's very unusual for such records to be so sparse on details. The scroll only vaguely alludes to two things.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Firstly, that the Bloomflower Trials were held to save a sick little saurian. Secondly, that they seem to have failed, and that the chief of the Flower-Feather Clan had a major falling out with his younger brother...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: And later on, his brother left the tribe and lived as a recluse. That's all it says.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But that basically tells us nothing! Y'know, except that the person who weaved this scroll must've been slacking off on the job!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Or maybe something happened that was too "sensitive" to record...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Sacred Flame Crystals having the power to "beguile human hearts"... Is this where that's from...?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Despite combing through the rest of the scrolls, none of you find any further references to the Bloomflower Trials.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Looks like we'll have to approach this from another angle...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I'll go take a look through some even older scrolls. Surely the Trials were held more than once...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Seeing as that scroll just now mentioned the Flower-Feather Clan, I think I could go ask Chief Mutota.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And what's our next move? Any other leads we can follow?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Come to think of it... That mysterious Qucusaur that Milray mentioned might be able to shed some light on this.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I have a feeling a certain Qucusaur might know a thing or two.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: A certain... Qucusaur? Who told you that?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Ahh, Ifa's assistant Cacucu must have told you, right? I heard he sometimes translates for the other saurians.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Yeah... This might not be the best time to dive into the whole saurian indwelling mystery. Guess I'll just give Cacucu the credit for now.)

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Alright, then. I'll look into those ancient scrolls, Kachina can head over to the Flower-Feather Clan, and you two can track down that Qucusaur.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Let's split up and meet back here later.

choices.text: First time I've ever heard that.

talks.objective: Ask Naiyan about the mysterious Qucusaur

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Naiyan, can you tell me any more about that mysterious Qucusaur you mentioned before?

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: Huh? You want to make friends with him too?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yup, that's right. Where can I find him?

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: Tracking him down's no easy task, because he's always off somewhere on his own. One second, he'll pop up in front of us, then vanish into thin air the next. It's actually pretty impressive...

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: One time, he took us to this absolutely beautiful place with this really, really tall stone gate.

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: And there were so many other Qucusaurs there! We wouldn't usually trespass on other saurians' territory, but since he took us there, it was fine. He said that was his home.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Qucusaurs and a stone gate... Sounds like it might be near the Flower-Feather Clan. Let's go check it out.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What does he look like? How will I recognize him?

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: He's really easy to spot — if you see one that looks all light and floaty, that's him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Light and... floaty?

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: Yep! Light and floaty. You'll know who he is the instant you see him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That seems to be the only description Naiyan can come up with. It's vague, but it'll have to do for now.)

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: Oh... And if you do see him, could you say hi from me and Milray? We're both starting to miss him... He did drop by to see us, but there were too many people around for his liking.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure thing, leave it to me.

talks.objective: Head to the location described by Naiyan

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Shhh... So everyone got that?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: They'll never see this coming. We'll catch them totally off guard!

dialogues.speaker: Iolana
dialogues.text: Leave it to us. We'll show them what we're made of!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mualani? Kinich? What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Aaaah!!!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: #Ohhh, {NICKNAME}, Paimon, it's you... Nearly scared the life out of me!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hehe, just between us, we're discussing our strategy for the next half of the exhibition match!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: But as for the details... those will have to stay a secret! After all, we'll be competing against you this time!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: What about you guys? You seem like you're in a hurry — has something happened?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're on the trail of an extremely rare and elusive Qucusaur...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Rare and elusive?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You give Kinich and Mualani a quick rundown on the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: In that case, we can help with the search!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: That description of the location's way too vague — the scenery around here's all pretty much the same. Without anyone to help out, it'll take you forever!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: What does the Qucusaur look like?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Light and floaty"...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Heh... Nothing more specific than that?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Apparently we'll know who he is the instant we see him.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Alright, well in that case, let's split up.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I'll check the higher ground and see if anyone over at the Flower-Feather Clan has any ideas.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I'll follow the river, then.

dialogues.speaker: Iolana
dialogues.text: Haha, sounds like it's my time to shine. As Kinich will tell you, I'm a born hunter with the eyes of a hawk.

dialogues.speaker: Tuqllaki
dialogues.text: I haven't got anywhere else to be, either. I'll take a stroll nearby and see if I can spot anything.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Awesome! Thanks, everyone!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Don't mention it. Anyway, we'd better get going. Catch you in a bit!

talks.objective: Ask the Qucusaurs nearby about the situation

dialogues.speaker: Cool-Headed Qucusaur
dialogues.text: That fruit just now was kinda sour...

dialogues.speaker: Energetic Qucusaur
dialogues.text: Try this one instead — it's super sweet!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Greetings, fellow saurians.

dialogues.speaker: Cool-Headed Qucusaur
dialogues.text: Hello there. How can we help?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I was just wondering... Have you ever met a Qucusaur around here who you'd describe as "light and floaty"?

dialogues.speaker: Cool-Headed Qucusaur
dialogues.text: Oh, you're talking about that kid, are ya?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Ehh? Are "light and floaty" really such distinct traits? These Qucusaurs seem to have instantly understood who I meant...)

dialogues.speaker: Cool-Headed Qucusaur
dialogues.text: He sometimes shows up around here, but he's always sneaking about, trying not to be seen.

dialogues.speaker: Energetic Qucusaur
dialogues.text: He's often perched up on a cliff, just gazing out on his lonesome, daydreaming about who knows what.

dialogues.speaker: Cool-Headed Qucusaur
dialogues.text: Oh yeah, and I'm pretty sure I saw him following a human around a couple of days back.

dialogues.speaker: Energetic Qucusaur
dialogues.text: Huh, well that's not something you see every day... He usually won't go anywhere near them.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So is there any way to get a hold of him?

dialogues.speaker: Cool-Headed Qucusaur
dialogues.text: I'd forget it if I were you. That kid comes and goes like a shadow.

dialogues.speaker: Energetic Qucusaur
dialogues.text: Come join us for some fruit instead! Haha... Come, try this one, sweet as sweet can be!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Okay... Thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Doesn't seem like a very "fruitful" lead... Guess I'd better wait and see if Mualani and Kinich have had any better luck.)

talks.objective: Meet up with Kinich and Mualani

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Anything on your end, Kinich?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Nope.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Me neither... Qucusaurs all look so similar.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: They all look "light and floaty" to me! I mean, what could possibly be lighter and floatier than a pair of wings?

dialogues.speaker: Iolana
dialogues.text: I didn't find anything either. How about you guys?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: #Sorry, {NICKNAME} and Paimon — we couldn't find that Qucusaur you're after.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Are you in a hurry to find him? If you need a hand, I can come back and join the search again tomorrow.

choices.text: Maybe he really is hiding from us...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Okay, well if you need any help, don't hesitate to reach out. That's what friends are for, after all!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: I've told my friends over at the Flower-Feather Clan to keep an eye out. If they see anything, they'll let you know. So, what's your next move?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I think we'll head back to the Masters of the Night-Wind.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Alright, I'll update them.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: ...Come to think of it, Ororon could probably rig up a few traps and snag him that way!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: It's not like Ororon's traps can catch just anything, you know...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: You never know! Might as well ask him if you get the chance. Anyway, we'll be heading back now — best of luck!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay then! See you later, and thanks for your help!

choices.text: I'll try to think of another way.

talks.objective: Return to the Masters of the Night-Wind

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hmm, let me think...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kachina! Citlali! What's up?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: We haven't managed to find anything. No one seems to know what actually happened back then.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Any luck with your mysterious Qucusaur?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: In that case... I'd suggest we set this aside for now.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: It would be great if we could get to the bottom of this, but not every historical mystery can be unraveled.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: We must also learn to live with the unknown. Just remember, as long as we stick together, no challenge will ever be too great.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Yeah, I'm sure everything will work out.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Still, after all this investigating, it feels a bit disappointing to come up empty-handed...

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: Whew... Finally, dudes! Found you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ifa! What brings you here?

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: Kinich mentioned you were on the lookout for a Qucusaur? Just so happens a strange Qucusaur has been following me the past few days.

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: No clue why, but this dude's been on my tail ever since I got back from the Children of Echoes. Not gonna lie to you bro, it's kinda freaky. His footsteps are totally silent, and after dark, all you can see is his silhouette...

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: So, I didn't even realize he was there until Cacucu suddenly flipped out last night when he went for a drink. His squawking woke me up, and that's when I finally spotted a shadowy shape outside the window.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That sounds terrifying!

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: I could tell it was a little Qucusaur from the shape. After observing him more closely, I figured out that he'd been following me the whole time, but that he'd just been too quiet to notice.

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: Not sure if that's the dude you're looking for, but if so, you're more than welcome to get him off my back — the sooner, the better!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: W—Wait a second, does that mean...

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: Yup, dude's probably hiding right behind that tree.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... D'you think we should send someone over to take a look?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: It's okay, I've got this...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: What the... How's that even...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Guys, get over here, quick! There's nothing scary about this, it's just...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Aah!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, surely that's not...
Coooo.... Cucuuuu...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (No wonder Naiyan described him as "light and floaty." He really is instantly recognizable — not like any Qucusaur I've ever seen.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (This must be Milray's mysterious friend, then. The one spreading the rumors about Sacred Flame Crystals "beguiling human hearts"...)

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Wait, shouldn't he have returned to the Ley Lines? Haven't they been fixed...?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: There are many possible reasons. But right now, it seems that our priority is...

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: Umm... So, why've you been tailing me, bro?

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: If it's treatment you want... Can't do much for you, man. Sorry.
Crooo...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: He ran off!
Craaawr!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do you think he... wants us to follow him?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If only we had our Qucu-Thesaurus on hand!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Hey, that's a good point. Where is Cacucu today?

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: He was so spooked last night that he rattled through every single word he's ever learned and then fainted. He was still out cold when I left.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Alright, enough chit-chat, let's just follow him. It looks like he wants to take us somewhere.

choices.text: Don't think it's planning to make an appearance anytime soon.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: *panting*... Looks like he's finally stopped.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Why have you brought us here?
Cooo...

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Sooo... Is there something buried here or what?
Guguu.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: You want us to dig it up?
Gruuuu!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After some energetic digging, you unearth an old, weathered box.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: These are...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Woven scrolls, yes. Albeit very crudely made, and heavily time-worn as a result.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Still, they're just about legible. They seem to document... the very last Bloomflower Trials that took place centuries ago!? But... why would these be here?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Come, let's read them together. These might just contain the answers we've been searching for this whole time.

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: So, have you figured out a way to save him?

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: Indeed I have. As far as I can tell, we need Ocean Zephyrs and Sacred Flame Crystals. That's about it.

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: That's great news. Don't worry, little guy. You'll be better in no time.
Crrawr...

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: Well, it's not every day that the Chief himself drops by to check in on your saurian buddy... Not so busy these days, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: Haha, you know I'd come even if I was. You're my brother, man! I heard you'd been beside yourself since Antu fell ill, so I was worried about you.

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: I mean, Antu means the world to me. I promised to stay by his side until the day he's fully grown, ready to spread his wings and soar freely through the skies.

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: I mean, with him around, I've never felt lonely traveling through Natlan. Sometimes he's happy, and other times he's sad. Sometimes he has tantrums, but then he'll curl up beside me when I'm down.

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: And right now, he needs me more than ever. I'll draw upon everything I've ever learned to help him get through this.

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: Craaawrr!

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: I salute your courage and wisdom, brother.

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: But these Sacred Flame Crystals you mentioned, are you sure they'll do the job?

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: Well, I've studied the essence of the Sacred Flame and read various related scrolls.

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: Sacred Flame Crystals are born from inter-tribal conflict. Back when the tribes were somewhat united, they would occasionally hold Bloomflower Trials in order to obtain them.

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: Hah, seems like I've still got lots to learn, despite being Chief... So, how can we use them? Is it really worth holding a whole competition just to get our hands on some?

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: Research on Sacred Flame Crystals has been patchy to say the least, so there's never been a definitive conclusion.

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: What we know for sure is that they can be used to treat certain chronic phlogiston-related illnesses. Others also say that they can be used to enhance a warrior's strength, or something.

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: ...Enhance a warrior's strength?

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: It's... speculative at best. We'd need to analyze an actual specimen to know for sure.

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: As far as I'm concerned, as long as they can be used to cure Antu's illness, that's enough. Nothing else matters.

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: So you asked the chiefs of all the tribes to send people to take part in a scaled-down version of the Bloomflower Trials?

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: Remarkable that they agreed, given it wasn't so long ago that we were at each other's throats.

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: Tensions are running high right now... If I were you, I wouldn't have had the courage to even ask.

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: I know, but I had no other choice. Fortunately, I've treated patients from every tribe, so the chiefs agreed as a way of returning the favor.

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: With all this ongoing strife, it's been a long time since we've worked together on anything. This might be a good chance for reconciliation.

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: Fighting side by side for a common cause... That's the way that Natlan was always meant to be.

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: Let's hope so. By the way, what's with all this baggage? Heading out on a long journey, or something?

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: I'm heading out to search for Ocean Zephyrs. In the meantime, I'll leave the Trials in your capable hands. Just please, make sure it all goes smoothly.

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: C'mon, that goes without saying! Rest assured — I'm your brother, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: Thank you. And Antu, be good while I'm gone, okay? Once I return with the ingredients, you'll be back on your feet and running around in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: Craaaa!

dialogues.speaker: Monetech
dialogues.text: Imara! How could you stoop so low, ambushing us on the field like that?

dialogues.speaker: Shanga
dialogues.text: Ambushing? You've no one but yourselves to blame for underestimating us, so what's all this fuss about?

dialogues.speaker: Paio
dialogues.text: Even if that was remotely true, your guys went way over the line! Seven of our warriors were so badly injured that they're still out cold as we speak!

dialogues.speaker: Paio
dialogues.text: The Flower-Feather Clan must compensate us for our losses. Hand over the Sacred Flame Crystals!

dialogues.speaker: Mbweni
dialogues.text: Pfft! And we'll hand 'em over after all that, just because you waggled some fingers and said some angry words?

dialogues.speaker: Monetech
dialogues.text: Didn't you claim that we're holding these Trials to save a sick saurian? Take what's necessary for the treatment, then return us the rest!

dialogues.speaker: Paio
dialogues.text: Say something, Imara! We're not leaving until you give us some answers!

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: Hmph! If the other elders were here, they wouldn't waste their time on such puerile questions.

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: If anything, I just wish we'd managed to collect more Crystals. There are always people who think they're so clever...

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: So many "contestants" were just pocketing the ones they got in the Trials. I'll bet your chiefs all have sweet little personal stashes too, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: Everyone was in a frenzy, snatching the Crystals up wherever and whenever they could. We're hardly the only winners. Heh, I wouldn't even call us the biggest ones.

dialogues.speaker: Monetech
dialogues.text: ...You what?

dialogues.speaker: Paio
dialogues.text: ...I get it now. Snatching the spoils while using the Bloomflower Trials to weaken the other tribes... You planned this all along!

dialogues.speaker: Paio
dialogues.text: Grr, that Nampole... Can't believe I trusted him...

dialogues.speaker: Monetech
dialogues.text: The Children of Echoes will not forget this. Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: ...Hmph.

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: Cooo?

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: Gruuu...

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: Brother, where's Antu?

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: Oh, you're back... Come, sit down, I'll explain everything—

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: No need for that. I only came back to ask... Are the rumors true?

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: Rumors? What rumors?

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: That the Bloomflower Trials spiraled into an all-out bloodbath, sparking a heated dispute among the chiefs.

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: And that no one was bothered in the slightest about Antu. By the time anyone noticed, he was already gone.

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: How could you lie to me, Imara? You promised you'd make sure the Bloomflower Trials went smoothly. Why would you resort to such underhanded tactics?

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: You think I had a choice? As soon as one person broke the rules, the whole thing became a free-for-all!

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: Playing by the rules gets you nowhere in this world. If I hadn't taken things into my own hands, another tribe would have just swooped in and seized the winnings for themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: These Sacred Flame Crystals... They have limitless potential! I, for one, wouldn't miss a chance to strengthen our tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: ...I won't debate ethics with you. Where are the Sacred Flame Crystals? Give me some, I'm going to search for Antu.

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: I've put them all into our research.

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: You did what!?

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: I did set some aside for Antu in the beginning. But he ran off, didn't he? So there was no longer any need.

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: He's your companion, yes, but the life of a single saurian is nothing compared to the future of our tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: ...Hear, hear! You've certainly proven yourself a worthy Chief, Imara. Your name will no doubt be etched into the hearts of the Flower-Feather Clan for generations to come.

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: Just remember this — no excuses can hide the harm your greed has inflicted.

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: All the hope and trust that that little guy placed in you, placed in me... You'll never know what that feels like!

dialogues.speaker: Imara
dialogues.text: Wait, Nampole! Where are you going?

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: Antu!

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: Antuuu...!

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: Antu, it's me! Please, answer me—

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: Guguuu?

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: Antu! Are you okay? Look at you, out here all on your own...

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: Guruuu...

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: I'm so sorry, Antu, this is all my fault. I'll think of another way...

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: (After that, I left the Flower-Feather Clan and lived here on this hill with Antu.)

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: (He was running out of time. I took him from tribe to tribe, begging them to spare some Sacred Flame Crystals... Our last hope.)

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: (But no one believed me anymore. I begged them again and again, enduring sneers, insults, even beatings...)

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: (Until finally, Antu's time came. In those last few days, he seemed consumed by an overwhelming sorrow, and then I realized — it wasn't just the sickness weighing him down, no. Remorse filled his gaze...)

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: (I remember once, over at the Children of Echoes, someone approached us with a Sacred Flame Crystal, flaunting it before quickly putting it away.)

dialogues.speaker: Monetech
dialogues.text: This is what you're after, is it? Hahaha, dream on!

dialogues.speaker: Monetech
dialogues.text: Go beg your brother for some! How many did he snatch up for himself? He's the one who put you up to this whole "I'm a victim" charade, wasn't he? I don't buy it!

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: Gruuuu!

dialogues.speaker: Monetech
dialogues.text: What are y...? You little vulture!

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: (For some reason, Antu harbored a deep and intense hatred for the Sacred Flame Crystals. Whenever he saw one, he would muster up every last ounce of his dwindling strength in trying to destroy it.)

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: (It wasn't until years after Antu's death that I finally guessed at the truth — he must've witnessed people fighting over the Crystals without comprehending why.)

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: (Unable to fathom how those once cheerful humans had turned from best of friends to worst of enemies, he concluded that they must have been corrupted by the Sacred Flame Crystals themselves.)

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: (In Antu's eyes, the only reason they'd started collecting Sacred Flame Crystals in the first place had been to save his life. "If I hadn't been there, none of this would have ever happened"... He carried this guilt with him until the very end.)

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: (I, too, shall be bound by guilt for the rest of my days. If only I had taken part in the Trials myself. If only I'd seen the greed in Imara's eyes, or even came back just a little bit sooner...)

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: (But the past cannot be undone. I have immersed myself in the study of medicine, and spent my life healing all kinds of saurians. I buried Antu here on this hill, where I too one day shall rest.)

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: (Before my own time comes, I've recorded all of this on these crudely woven scrolls in the belief that the truth should not lie buried. May those who come long after us learn from our errors, lest they repeat them.)

dialogues.speaker: Nampole
dialogues.text: (May the Natlan of their day be united as one, free once and for all from bloodshed and strife...)

talks.objective: Talk to Ifa and the others

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: "Medicine born of guilt"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, the Nampole from the scrolls was Ifa's ancestor? And that little Qucusaur spirit was once his saurian companion?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Seems so. That's why he's been following you around, Ifa, even though he doesn't like appearing in front of anyone else — he senses something familiar in you.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: No wonder there weren't any records of the last Bloomflower Trials. If anything corrupts the human heart, it's greed... And who'd want to immortalize the memory of a scandal by which all six tribes were tainted?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The bitter irony is that Sacred Flame Crystals turned out to be nowhere near as miraculous as they'd believed... All that scheming, after what proved to be nothing more than a hollow fantasy.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Hey, where's that little Qucusaur gone?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, over there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: D'you think he's sad? Or maybe he's lost in his memories...

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: Thanks... Might need a breather over here...

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: A regret lingering for centuries, unfolding like this before my eyes... Can't believe I'm just now hearing my ancestor's story. Now I know why we became vets, too...

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: I gotta think this through. What should I do? What can I even do...

choices.text: I'll go hang out with him for a bit.

talks.objective: Talk to the little Qucusaur Antu

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Antu.

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: #Aaaah! You're... Huh? Aren't you the {M#blond guy}{F#blonde gal} from just now?

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: Wait... Is this your real form? You can turn yourself into a human? That's amazing! Can you teach me how you do it? I want to talk to the humans, but they don't like me...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you still remember what happened back then?

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: Only bits and pieces...

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: I remember being in a lot of pain. I remember how worried my good friend Nampole was. Afterwards, the pain stopped, and my body felt so light... but I couldn't find him anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: I hid, and searched... Hid, and searched... I searched without end... My body kept getting colder and colder, like I was freezing to death.

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: Luckily, I found a nice, cozy cave, where I huddled up and slept for ages. When I woke back up again, the world seemed completely different.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A cave?

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: Yeah, and there were all these strange patterns on the walls. Some of them even looked a bit like me!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Could he mean the Remnants of the Secret Source? That's the closest place to the Night Kingdom... Maybe his soul hasn't faded away yet because he was "hibernating" there...)

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: When I came out of the cave, I saw that those evil monsters had returned, so I went to help — that's how I met Milray and Naiyan.

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: The three of us had them running in circles, haha! Once I'd showed my friends the way, those monsters didn't stand a chance of catching them.

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: Eventually, those monsters all disappeared, and then I faintly heard the sound of Nampole's voice, calling out for me to come to him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The monsters disappeared... This must have been after the final battle against the Abyss. The Ley Lines had been restored, so at this point, he could've returned to the Night Kingdom.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But you didn't go to him?

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: I wanted to, but then Milray came down with the same illness I had, and I was so worried for him... Nampole said that Sacred Flame Crystals were required for the cure, but those Crystals are evil!

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: As soon as they got their hands on them, even the closest of friends would get into the most vicious arguments. Everyone started acting so strangely... Like they'd all been bewitched!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So... You think it was all caused by the Sacred Flame Crystals?

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: What else could it have been? They were all such good friends before, and they used to care about me, too...

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: It's all because of those evil Crystals! I wish I could cast every last one of them into a volcano! But we need them to cure Milray... What should we do?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Just as Nampole concluded in his scroll, Antu misunderstood the real cause of the strife... It wasn't the power of Sacred Flame Crystals to bewitch human hearts, but rather, human greed and scheming.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (But... What can we do now for this poor little creature? Should I tell him the truth? From his standpoint, would knowing the truth even make any difference?)

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: #What's wrong, {M#big bro} {F#big sis}? You seem a bit down.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm okay...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's head back to where the others are.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Antu's eyes are full of such heartfelt concern... I don't know what to tell him. The times have changed, and so have the people. He's the only one still trapped in the past...)

talks.objective: Meet up with Ifa and the others

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Never thought I'd have the chance to meet my ancestor's saurian companion... It's a pretty cool feeling.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Wouldn't you say so, bro?

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: Coooo?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Can he understand what you're saying?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Kinda. I can pick up on Antu's vibes, just like he catches ours... But that's pretty much it.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: That's just how it is with saurian companions, you have to spend a lot of time together to develop an intuitive bond. If my ancestor were here, I'm sure they'd vibe way easier.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: In other words, he wouldn't understand even if we discussed everything that went on back then in front of him, right? ... *sigh* I'm not even sure if that's a good thing or a bad thing.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I... think it's probably better if he doesn't understand.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I know that running from your problems isn't the way to solve them, and that we should face up to the challenges in our lives. But even if we told him the truth... Wouldn't it only distress him more than he already is?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: That's right. The people responsible, the ones who should have apologized to him, are no longer around. All the truth would do is tear open old wounds and sadden him all over again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Isn't there anything we could do to help him forget his sorrow and find hope once more?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Just like Nampole, I've spent a lot of time studying saurian psychology.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: They can be a bit slow sometimes, but they're razor sharp at others. They don't get complex human language, but they get a lot just from reading our eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: In short, young saurians are just like children. On one hand, they rely on their human companions. On the other, they really want to prove their worth. Helping people makes them happy, and feeling like a burden makes them sad.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: So... The best move isn't to get stuck on the truth of what happened, but to help make his current wishes come true.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: His wishes?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: For example...

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Antu, you decided to stay here because of Milray and Naiyan, right?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: You're a smart kid. Sacred Flame Crystals are bad, bad things that cause endless arguments among good friends.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: But now, after hundreds of years, we've finally found a way to beat 'em.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Will you join forces with us to cleanse the evil inside them so we can save your buddy together?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Interesting approach... You want to turn a lie into the truth, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Antu
dialogues.text: Guguu?

choices.text: Never mind what you're trying to do...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Actually, uh, I... I didn't really understand either! Is there really some kind of evil power inside the Sacred Flame Crystals...?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Oh, dear child...! Come, come, let Granny explain it to you.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The group has a quick strategy huddle...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Ohhhh, I get it now! Okay, I'll do my best!

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: Not so fast. Hate to break it to you, but the three of us can't make this happen.

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: Let's meet up at the Stadium in two days. We'll spread the word and see who's willing to play along.

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: As for making Antu understand... Uh, Cacucu can help out. They'll have an easier time communicating.

choices.text: ...Can we even be sure he understood you?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'll find some time to take these scrolls back to the Masters of the Night-Wind. Just like Nampole said, the truth shouldn't stay buried.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Poor Antu...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Chief Mutota!

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Kachina? What brings you here?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: We're looking into what happened the last time the Bloomflower Trials were held. It seems the then-chief of the Flower-Feather Clan got into an argument with his brother... Do you know anything about that?

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Sorry... I'm afraid that was all so long ago... I haven't heard anything about this either.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Doesn't feel like there are any leads we can follow up on here...

dialogues.speaker: Milray
dialogues.text: Thanks for coming to see me, Ayo.

dialogues.speaker: Ayo
dialogues.text: How are you feeling, Milray?

dialogues.speaker: Milray
dialogues.text: I'm feeling... dizzy... Think I need to sleep a while longer...

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: Milray...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (There seem to be quite a few Qucusaurs living around here... I'll try asking them.)

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You follow the little Qucusaur spirit, who leads you much further away than you'd expected...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The spirit of the Qucusaur chick Antu stands quietly on the hillside. Unlike Milray, the Tepetlisaur whelp who's loved by humans and saurian alike, Antu stands utterly alone, detached from both heaven and earth...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (As he was in life, so he remains in death. What might he be thinking? It's time I went and asked him.)
